function.mechanism: Acts as part of the sulfite preservative system; inferred to reduce oxidative/enzymatic browning and inhibit spoilage reactions in susceptible foods.

adi.basis: EFSA 2022 follow-up withdrew the temporary group ADI (previously 0.7 mg SO2 equivalents/kg bw/day).

efsa.key_finding: EFSA concluded the toxicity database was inadequate to derive an ADI and identified safety concern under assessed exposure scenarios using an MOE approach.

fda.cfr_citation: No specific listing for calcium hydrogen sulfite/calcium bisulfite found in fetched 21 CFR Title 21 eCFR data; related sulfites: 21 CFR 182.3616, 182.3637, 182.3739, 182.3766, 182.3862.

adi.basis: Group ADI 0-0.7 mg/kg bw expressed as sulfur dioxide for sulfur dioxide-sulfite compounds including calcium hydrogen sulfite.

concerns.summary: Patch-test-positive sodium disulfite patients reported more frequent systemic symptoms after high-sulfite foods versus controls in a 2025 retrospective study.
In vitro human lymphocyte data (2025) reported increased chromosomal aberrations/micronuclei for sodium sulfite at higher concentrations.
EFSA 2022 follow-up withdrew temporary ADI and identified MOE-based safety concern for sulfur dioxide/sulfites (including E227) under assessed dietary scenarios.

no_concern_confirmed: A 2016 rat dietary study did not reproduce previously reported gastric lesions from sodium metabisulfite exposure (PMID:27401986).
Some national dietary exposure assessments found average intake below ADI in many groups (e.g., PMID:19680935, PMID:28959578).

populations: High-intake consumers in some dietary scenarios
Most population groups in EFSA 2022 assessed scenarios (except adolescents in one refined high-percentile scenario)
adi_exceedance.notes: EFSA 2022 MOEs were below the comparison value in multiple groups/scenarios; some country studies also reported potential high-intake exceedance scenarios.

risk_assessment.rationale: The latest EFSA follow-up (2022) could not maintain an ADI and identified safety concern in assessed exposure scenarios, which matches the provided high-tier trigger ('EFSA unable to confirm safety').
key_factors: EFSA 2022 follow-up withdrew temporary ADI and applied MOE approach with concern signal
IARC classification is Group 3 (does not independently elevate carcinogenic tier)
Human sensitivity/allergy-related symptom signals exist in susceptible groups
Specific US CFR listing for calcium hydrogen sulfite was not identified in retrieved Title 21 data
